Anchor.description:
Where a zone's text comes from in the source the set was read from: characters ``[start, end)`` of the source
text (``Source.uri`` / ``Source.record`` at ``Source.revision``).
Anchor.title: Anchor

AnnotationSet.description: Everything one source said about one page.
AnnotationSet.title: AnnotationSet

Annotator.description:
One thing that worked on an annotation set: a model step, a rule-based step, a delivered file, or people.
``measurements`` keys come from the fixed vocabulary ``linecaster.data.MEASUREMENTS``. ``linecaster``: the
linecaster that recorded it (``producer``; set by ``Transcription.add_annotator``), so a record names its writer
wherever it travels.
Annotator.title: Annotator

Cell.description:
One cell of a table: its rows and columns (offsets, end exclusive), its text and whether it heads a column, a
row or a section. ``formulas``: where the source marks a formula in the cell (MathML, a wiki's ``<math>``), its
character span in ``text`` ([start, end), the ``$…$`` the text writes it as included); a ``$`` outside them is
printed. Empty where the source marks none or cannot say (an engine's HTML that writes ``$…$`` as text).
Cell.title: Cell

Classification.description: One value of one scheme for one target; a ``status`` may say why (``reason``, one of ``REASONS``).
Classification.title: Classification

Decision.description:
One decision of a recomposition, at one row of a paragraph (``row``: the index into ``Paragraph.rows``): where
a paragraph breaks, and where it runs on (what joins the pieces is the output strategy's, ``flow``).
Decision.title: Decision

Description.description: Text an annotator wrote about a zone that is not on the page (a description of a picture, a summary).
Description.title: Description

DocumentRange.description: A document within or across items; ``kind`` is always written (``kind="document"``).
DocumentRange.title: DocumentRange

Edit.description: Another form of a target's text, as the source states it; the target's own text (the literal) stays.
Edit.title: Edit

Formatting.description:
How characters ``charspan`` of a reading's text are set: bold, italic, underlined, struck through, raised or
lowered.
Formatting.title: Formatting

source.description: the LaTeX as the source wrote it, where the reading's differs (a wiki's formula as its software normalizes it)
source.title: Source

Line.description: A line zone, with the region it was assigned to and, once recognized, its reading.
Line.title: Line

PageImage.description:
The image a page's coordinates refer to. Bytes travel next to the row (``Document.media``),
never inside it.
PageImage.title: PageImage

Paragraph.title: Paragraph

ParagraphRow.description: One visual row of a paragraph: every line on the row.
ParagraphRow.title: ParagraphRow

Range.description:
A logical unit of content: its piece on this page. Pieces with the same id on other pages of the item are
the same range.
Range.title: Range

RawOutput.description: One request's answer, verbatim: a completion as the model wrote it, or an engine's native result.
RawOutput.title: RawOutput

Reading.description: What a recognizer read on one line: exactly as the engine produced it.
Reading.title: Reading

ReadingOrder.description:
An order of the page: its regions in reading order, its lines in reading order, and each of those lines'
visual row within its region (``rows``, parallel to ``lines``). An order of regions only leaves ``lines`` empty.
ReadingOrder.title: ReadingOrder

Region.description: A zone from a layout step; ``label`` is the annotator's own, verbatim.
Region.title: Region

Source.description: Where an annotation set comes from: produced here, converted from a delivered file, or a ground truth.
Source.title: Source

Table.description: A region's table structure; ``html`` as the model wrote it, when it did.
Table.title: Table

Transcription.description: An annotation set that also holds text: OCR, HTR or ground truth of one page.
Transcription.title: Transcription

Word.description: A word of a reading. ``id`` only when its source gave one other than ``<line>_w<n>``.
Word.title: Word
